Search terms for this lesson“how do I make a double jump?”Outline only

Short lesson (~15 min) + Cave Level / Boss Prep Studio. In 6.2 you built jumpsRemaining and maxJumps = 1 inside PlayerController. Today we move both integers into StatManager so a double jump (maxJumps = 2) persists across scenes and respawns — then spend the rest of Friday finishing your cave before Thanksgiving Break.

Break It Down~10 minOutline only

Move the jump counter onto StatManager so multi-jump upgrades persist everywhere and unlock double jumping.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Move jumpsRemaining and maxJumps into StatManagerwhat does this part do?Read: 5.3 (StatManager singleton + public fields vs private fields with methods)
  2. Point PlayerController at manager.jumpsRemaining and manager.maxJumpswhat does this part do?Read: 6.2 (Start(), Update(), and OnCollisionEnter2D() inside PlayerController.cs)

In 6.2 we put jumpsRemaining and maxJumps on PlayerController, which resets every time a scene loads. Moving them into StatManager works identically for health and coins: StatManager (DontDestroyOnLoad) remembers whether you unlocked a double jump (maxJumps = 2) across every door and respawn.

Your turn

Pick two of the parts above and say in one line what each one actually does.

Look at StatManager.cs: health, maxHealth, and coins have NO public keyword, so why did PlayerController need manager.ChangeHealth() and manager.ChangeCoins() — and what happens if you move jumpsRemaining and maxJumps onto StatManager without marking them public?

Once jumpsRemaining and maxJumps live on StatManager, which three places in PlayerController.cs need manager. added in front of them (and where do you still reset manager.jumpsRemaining = manager.maxJumps)?

In the Code: Move Jump State to StatManager (~10 min) ~10 min
ScriptWhat moves / changesWhy
StatManager.cs Add public int jumpsRemaining; and public int maxJumps = 1; (or set maxJumps = 2 when testing / unlocking boots) C# fields default to private; adding public (or public helper methods) lets PlayerController read and update jump count across scripts, while DontDestroyOnLoad() keeps unlocks alive.
PlayerController.cs Remove local jumpsRemaining / maxJumps; update Start(), Update(), and OnCollisionEnter2D() to use manager.jumpsRemaining and manager.maxJumps Keeps one source of truth instead of two competing copies of the counter.
Optional Upgrade Pickup In OnTriggerEnter2D(), check a tag (e.g. "Boots") to run manager.maxJumps = 2; manager.jumpsRemaining = manager.maxJumps; Destroy(other.gameObject); Reuses the exact coin-pickup pattern from 2.1 to unlock a permanent double jump.
Check your entry scene when testing: if you press Play inside Platformer directly, make sure there is a StatManager in the scene (or launch from Start (index 0)) so manager = FindAnyObjectByType<StatManager>(); never returns null.

Socratic: Ownership & Multi-Jump Data

  1. In 6.2 you had to change 0 jump lines inside Update() or OnCollisionEnter2D() to turn single jump into double jump besides changing which object owns maxJumps. Why does storing a count instead of a bool canJump scale to 2, 3, or 5 jumps for free?
  2. What happens in C# if you move jumpsRemaining onto StatManager as int jumpsRemaining; without typing public?
  3. When the player dies and StatManager.Die() reloads the current scene, does a Boots pickup (manager.maxJumps = 2) stay unlocked or disappear? Contrast that with how coins behave in Die().
In the Editor + Studio: Finish Cave & Prep for Boss Week (~55 min) ~55 min
  1. Test manager.maxJumps = 2 directly on StatManager (or via a "Boots" pickup in your cave), verify two jumps work mid-air, and confirm touching "Ground" refills both.
  2. Audit every high platform or gap in Platformer.unity: decide which jumps require single-jump + moving platforms/ladders and which secret areas reward a double jump.
  3. Playtest the whole progression from Overworld → Platformer → end-of-cave boss doorway, and commit + push before Thanksgiving Break.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain why moving jumpsRemaining and maxJumps onto StatManager keeps double jump state alive across scenes
  • Use public fields (or public methods) cleanly so PlayerController reads and resets manager.jumpsRemaining
  • Verify double jump resets on "Ground" collision and never allows a third air jump
  • Leave your cave playable and ready for independent Boss Fight building after Thanksgiving
  • Commit and push
